title: docs: name the canonical docs host in the governed protection examples
body:
Fixes #10656

Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-21, verbatim and untranslated:

> 这个仓的文档站规范 URL 是 https://objectstack.ai

## Re-measurement vs the card

Re-grepped the whole tree for `docs.objectstack.ai` at my HEAD and worked from that, not
from the card's line numbers. **The card's counts hold exactly** — 5 occurrences across 3
governed paths, no drift, despite the data SKILL.md having been edited since the card was
filed. Only the SKILL.md line numbers moved (the card gave none for that file).

| Site | Card | Measured | Disposition |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--|
| `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` | 3 | 3 (L898, L916, L937) | **fixed** |
| `docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md` | 1 (`:565`) | 1 (`:565`) | **fixed** |
| `docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md` | 1 (`:85`) | 1 (`:85`) | **kept unchanged** — argued below |

No other governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`) carries the spelling. The remaining tree hits are all outside the register —
`CHANGELOG.md` history, the three landed `.changeset/` entries that describe this very
convergence, and `scripts/check-published-readme-links.mjs`, which must keep naming the
alias because it is the detector that classifies it.

## The host was only half the defect

All four fixed occurrences are the **same literal**, and a pure host swap would have left
a dead URL behind. The landed changeset `canonical-docs-host-in-runtime-strings.md` states
the finding in full:

> All 29 `protection.docsUrl` values on the platform's system objects and apps pointed at
> `/adr/0010-metadata-protection`, and `/adr/...` is not a route on any host: the docs site
> mounts `content/docs` under `/docs`, `docs/adr/` is not published, and no redirect source
> lives outside the `/docs` space. The slug was wrong too — the record is
> `0010-metadata-protection-model.md`.

So the correct target is not a guess — it is pinned three ways by work that has already
landed: the 29 platform sources, the `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts` docblock
example, and the changeset's own reasoning. Every changed line becomes:

```ts
docsUrl: 'https://objectstack.ai/docs/references/shared/protection',
```

Diff discipline held: **4 changed lines, each containing `docs.objectstack.ai` before and
`objectstack.ai` after.** No prose reworded, no reflowing, no drive-by fixes.

## Per-site disposition

### 1. `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` ×3 — fixed (the propagating surface)

Three `protection` blocks in worked examples (`sys_user`, `sys_role`, `setup.app`) that
mirror three real platform files, all three of which already landed on the canonical
literal. This is the surface that travels: the published skill catalog lands in codebases
this repo cannot see, so the skill teaching `/adr/0010-metadata-protection` would keep
minting a 404 into AI-authored `protection` blocks long after the source was fixed.

### 2. `docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md:565` — fixed (a stale quotation)

The card flagged this as possibly quoting the code that #10655 covered. It is: the fenced
`ts` block at §Phase 4.3 is a **verbatim quotation** of the `SETUP_APP` example in
`packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`. Diffing the two blocks, the `docsUrl` line was
their *only* divergence — every other byte matched. #10655 closed 2026-08-21T23:57, so the
card's own condition ("it should move *with* the code, not ahead of it") is satisfied, and
this one line now restores byte-identity with the source it quotes.

This is not a rewording under PD #13: the recorded decision (a `protection` block carrying
`docsUrl`) is untouched. Only the illustration was stale, and a stale quotation makes the
ADR misdocument its own implementation.

### 3. `docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md:85` — KEPT UNCHANGED

The card suspected this one describes a past state deliberately. Reading the surrounding
section confirms it. The line sits in **§2 Goals & Non-goals → Non-goals**:

> - **Standalone product doc sites** (docs.objectstack.ai) — those are
>   websites; `content/docs/` remains their convention.

Two reasons to leave it:

1. **It is not a URL.** No scheme, no markdown link, no autolink — the hostname is an
   identifying parenthetical whose job is to say *which category of thing* is out of scope
   for `doc` metadata. Nobody follows it or copies it. The ruling governs the canonical docs
   *URL*; this is not one.
2. **It is decision prose.** A Non-goals bullet is the ADR's recorded scope boundary, dated
   2026-06-12 — more than two months before the canonical ruling. **Prime Directive #13**:

   > **An accepted ADR binds until a superseding ADR says otherwise.** Reversing a recorded
   > decision is itself a decision: it needs a **new ADR** (or an amended status line on the
   > old one), not a changeset that quietly does the opposite.

   Editing the sentence would be silently rewording a decision record for zero user-facing
   effect. The reference also remains unambiguous: the alias still redirects to the apex
   path-preservingly, per the landed changeset.

If the maintainer would rather this line track the canonical spelling too, that is an ADR
amendment and belongs in its own change — not smuggled in under a link fix.

## Token budget — `skills/**` readings

The dispatch requires both readings for any `skills/**` diff, and this file sits under
`check:skills-token-ratchet` at ceiling **13817 with zero headroom**.

**The change is exactly byte-neutral** — the two literals are both 56 bytes, so nothing was
spent and nothing was reclaimed:

| `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (lines) | 1210 | 1210 | **0** |
| `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (bytes) | 55265 | 55265 | **0** |
| `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (tokens) | 13817 | 13817 | **0** |
| Whole published package, all 11 `SKILL.md` (bytes) | 471666 | 471666 | **0** |
| Whole published package (tokens) | 117922 | 117922 | **0** |

No prose was deleted to pay for anything, and **no ceiling was raised** (maintainer-only).

### Governed verdict on the final file list

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`

```
governed-surface predicate: 2 of 2 path(s) hit the register (5 surfaces, repo-agnostic).
  ⛔  GOVERNED — a human merge is the review record for this PR (#9495 regime).
      No seat flips it ready, enqueues it, or arms auto-merge (AGENTS.md Prime Directive #14).
      One hit governs the whole PR — 「混合 diff 一条命中即整 PR 分叉」; proportion is not a question.
      docs/adr/** ×1 — architecture decision records
        - docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md
      skills/** ×1 — the published skills catalog
        - skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md
```

**This PR stays a draft and is merged by the maintainer by hand.** Not flipped ready, not
enqueued, no auto-merge. Assigned to `os-zhuang` for review (review-request fails on a
self-authored PR).

## Changeset

None, by the changeset gate's own prescription. `pr-automation.yml` lists the paths that
release nothing — `.github/`, `.claude/`, **`skills/`**, **`docs/`**, `content/` — and its
error text says such a PR takes the label rather than a file:

> This PR adds no changeset. If it releases nothing (including any `skills/**` change — see
> #5947), apply the `skip-changeset` label

`skills/` is not a workspace member and no package's `files` field ships it, so nothing here
publishes. The `skip-changeset` label is applied additively (POST, never a wholesale PUT)
and read back — the size labeler's PUT is documented to race it away.
